result.summary: Extracts arbitrary-parent block template reconstruction into a shared RebuildBlockForParent test helper used by BuildChain and MinerTestingSetup::Block. The helper updates the header hash and timestamp, recalculates the proof-of-work target and block subsidy from the target parent, appends a dummy OP_0 to satisfy minimum coinbase script length on low heights, and asserts coinbase-only templates.
result.problem: Test utilities creating fork blocks by repointing active-tip templates could retain the active tip's work target or subsidy, and produced coinbase scripts below the minimum length requirement at heights 1 through 16. Existing test callers either avoided these boundary conditions or worked around them locally, but new tests constructing forks could produce invalid blocks.
evidence: PR description: 'test helpers attaching active-tip block templates to arbitrary parents could retain the wrong work target or subsidy. Rebuilding the coinbase input script for heights 1 through 16 without padding also produces a script below the minimum length. Existing callers avoid these cases or handle them locally, so no current test fails.'
Commit 15ffe40719: 'Current chain-building callers use regtest with retargeting disabled, so this prevents future invalid test cases rather than fixing an existing failure.'
result.changed_since_previous: Enforced coinbase-only templates by asserting block.vtx.size() == 1 in RebuildBlockForParent and passing use_mempool = false in MinerTestingSetup::Block to prevent fee stripping when rewriting coinbase subsidies.
result.card: PR #36109 unifies block reconstruction logic for arbitrary-parent test helpers (BuildChain and MinerTestingSetup::Block) into a shared RebuildBlockForParent helper. It recalculates the parent-dependent work target and block subsidy, pads coinbase scriptSigs with OP_0 to satisfy length requirements at heights 1-16, and enforces coinbase-only templates so fee rewards cannot be silently overwritten. The author notes no existing tests fail today because current callers avoid these edge cases, making this preventative test harness hardening.

risk.why: Touches only unit test utilities and test cases without affecting consensus, node, or production code.
